exposure: endometrial defects at caesarean scars (in situ haemorrhage, bloody mucus, epithelial deficiency, exposed blood vessels, hyperplastic vessels, endometrial thickness, local vascularization, plasma cell count)
myometrial CSD defects (diverticulum sizes, CSD size, number of previous caesarean sections)
cohort: The study included 155 patients with caesarean scar defects (CSDs), initially separated into groups with and without abnormal uterine bleeding (AUB), and then 30 AUB patients matched with 30 non-AUB patients based on CSD size and number of previous caesarean sections.
finding: Endometrial defects at caesarean scars contribute more significantly to abnormal uterine bleeding (AUB) than myometrial defects.
mod_finding: The study directly investigates sequelae of caesarean section, finding that endometrial defects at caesarean scars are a significant contributor to abnormal uterine bleeding.
